question:
A 25-year-old male seeks medical attention from his primary care physician due to constipation lasting
6 days. The symptoms began one day after he started using an over-the-counter medication to treat
sinus congestion and persistent cough. He reports no other associated symptoms. His medical history
reveals only seasonal allergies, and he denies using any medications other than the recently started
over-the-counter remedy. Which medication is the most likely cause of his current symptoms? Answer
Choices: (A) Cetirizine (B) Brompheniramine (C) Acetaminophen (D) Pseudoephedrine (E)
Dextromethorphan (F) Guaifenesin (G) Phenylephrine (H) Loratadine (I) Chlorpheniramine (J)
Diphenhydramine
 A. Brompheniramine
B. Cetirizine
C. Acetaminophen
D. Loratadine
E. Guaifenesin
F. Dextromethorphan
G. Phenylephrine
H. Pseudoephedrine
I. Chlorpheniramine
J. Diphenhydramine
